title: Byte on Nova’s PRs and the panel

story: Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, opens draft PR #2512 for RH-1234 and waits for Byte, our review agent, because Nova only marks a PR ready when Byte's review is clean. Nothing happens. fcp's workflow and Byte's gate both skip draft PRs, so Byte never looks, and Nova would wait until its waiting time runs out.

Now imagine Byte does review it, the way it reviews people's PRs. It posts seven comments: one about a problem Nova had already listed in its own self-review, two style notes, one naming idea, and three real problems. A person would read all seven, fix three and ignore the rest. Nova treats every inline comment as a task: seven fixes, seven replies, a new push, a new review with new notes, another round.
hook.question: How does Byte review Nova's drafts so that every comment it posts is worth a fix?

p: Byte skips drafts for a good reason: people open drafts while they are still working, and a review then is noise. Nova's drafts are different, because Nova keeps the PR in draft exactly until Byte's review is clean. So we make one narrow exception, in two places. fcp's workflow that calls Byte starts a review when a PR is opened, drafts included, only if its author is rhino-ai-agents[bot], the GitHub App every agent uses. Without that guard, every human PR would get a full review the moment it is opened.

Byte's gate then accepts the event only if the PR's author and the sender of the event are both in a short list of agent authors, the PR targets main, and the PR body has a Requested-by: line naming a person who has write access today. That line names whoever handed Nova the ticket. It matters because the App itself is not a collaborator: someone with real access must answer for the PR. The gate reads the body from GitHub at that moment, not from the event, so an old copy cannot be replayed. Later pushes go through the sniff, Byte's very cheap check of whether old findings were fixed, as for people, so Nova's fix pushes cost a cheap check, not a full review.

notes.text: Three conditions: an agent author, the agent itself sent the event, and the base is main.
The login after Requested-by: @ in the live PR body.
No requester, no review: someone must answer for an agent's PR.
Write access is checked now, so a person who left the team cannot be the requester.

read.h: The receipt is data, not orders
p: Before Nova opens the PR, a fresh self-reviewer (a second model session that never saw Nova's reasoning) reads its diff and Nova writes a receipt into the PR body, such as "found 6, fixed 5, left 1, because …". Byte reads that receipt, so it does not post a problem Nova has already explained. A finding that matches an issue the receipt lists as known and still open is marked known, and known findings are counted, not posted.

But the receipt is text written by an agent that read tickets and code from other people, and any text in a PR can carry instructions meant for an AI reviewer. So the receipt can never make a finding disappear. If the receipt says an issue is fixed, Byte drops its finding only when the code at head shows the fix. Text in the PR can mark something as known; only the code can mark it as fixed. The same rule covers every file in the PR: Byte's playbooks are baked into its image, and a REVIEW.md or a comment inside the PR never steers it.

read.h: Post only what Nova should act on
p: On people's PRs Byte posts every finding. On agent PRs, only new high and medium findings go inline. Low findings, and findings the receipt already listed, are counted instead, in one small table in Byte's check run: posted inline, known from the receipt, and counted only, by severity. Nothing disappears silently, but Nova only gets the comments it should fix.

Some kinds of finding are noise for a whole team. Each finding now carries a category from a fixed list (correctness, security, data-loss, performance, convention, test-gap, docs, naming, style). When people give a category a thumbs-down on at least 30% of its findings, over at least 20 findings, a reviewed PR adds it to that team's quiet categories, and on agent PRs those findings are counted too. A high-severity security or data-loss finding is never quiet, whatever people think of the category.

notes.text: People's PRs: unchanged, every finding is posted.
Quiet, unless it is a high security or data-loss finding.
Known from the receipt: counted, not posted.
Low: counted, not posted. Nova should not spend a round on a nit.

deeper.h: Go deeper: quiet categories pass the gate too
p: The thumbs-down rate per team and category comes from the weekly job that gives every finding a fate (the previous lesson). A change to quietCategories is a change to Byte's policy file, so it runs the BYTE-GOLD gate like any other: a category may only be quieted if doing so costs no recall on high bugs. From the second review round on, Byte's existing rule already holds findings on unchanged code to high severity only, so later rounds stay short.

read.h: The panel: many lenses, then a skeptic
p: For risky PRs, deep mode runs the panel. A lens is one separate, read-only Claude session with one job: correctness, security, conventions, past incidents, or requirements. Separate sessions let each lens focus, and let BYTE-GOLD score each lens on its own. Three lenses are blind: correctness, security and conventions read only the diff and the code, never the PR body or Nova's plan, because a reviewer who reads the author's plan tends to check the plan instead of the code. Only the requirements lens reads the PR's title and body, to compare the change with what was asked.

A reviewer told to find problems always finds some, so five lenses produce too much. After removing duplicates, a skeptic session takes each finding and tries to prove it wrong. It must answer confirmed, refuted or unsure, and cite the file and line that prove its answer. Code checks the cite: the file must exist in the checkout and the line must be inside it. A confirmed answer with a cite that does not hold counts as unsure. Refuted findings are dropped, unsure ones are lowered one step in severity and confidence, and whatever is left is ranked and posted through the usual path.

notes.text: path:line, and no .. in the path, so the skeptic cannot point outside the checkout.
The line must exist in that file. A cite to line 400 of a 120-line file does not hold.
Confirmed without real evidence is treated as unsure.
Unsure: one step down. The confidence filter later drops what falls to low confidence.

deeper.h: Go deeper: how the panel is run
p: The runner fetches the diff once through the broker into a file. The blind lenses get Read, Glob and Grep on the checkout and that file, and no gh command at all, so they cannot fetch the PR body. Correctness, security, incidents and requirements run on Opus 5.5 at medium effort; conventions runs on Sonnet 5.5 at low. The conventions lens reads Byte's own team playbooks. The incidents lens reads a list of bug classes copied from the incident pages of the brain, our repo of pages about how our systems work, by a reviewed PR, never fetched while reviewing, and naming classes, not PRs.

Duplicates are found in code first: same file, same title once lowercased and stripped of punctuation, and lines within 5 of each other. The higher severity wins, then the higher confidence, then the lens in the order security, correctness, requirements, incidents, conventions. The skeptic then runs on at most 15 findings, 4 at a time, on Opus 5.5 at medium. The survivors are ranked by severity and confidence and capped at 25, with "+N more below the cut" in the summary. The run records, per lens, how many findings were raised, refuted and kept, so BYTE-GOLD shows what each lens and the skeptic add.

check.q: Nova's receipt says an issue is fixed. Byte's review still finds that issue in the code at head. What happens?

options.text: The finding is dropped, because the receipt says fixed
options.why: Text in a PR can never remove a finding. Only the code at head can show the fix.

options.text: The finding is marked known and counted
options.why: Known is for issues the receipt lists as still open. This one is claimed fixed and is not.

options.text: The finding stays, and is posted if it is a new high or medium one
options.why: The code shows the issue is still there, so Nova must fix it.

check.q: Why do the correctness, security and conventions lenses never see the PR body?

options.text: A reviewer who reads the author's plan tends to check the plan instead of the code
options.why: Blind lenses judge the diff on its own, and they also cannot be steered by text in the body.

options.text: The body is too long for their context
options.why: Length is not the reason. Independence from the author's story is.

options.text: Only the skeptic is allowed to use gh
options.why: The skeptic reads the checkout too. The requirements lens is the one that reads the body.

check.q: The skeptic answers confirmed for a high finding and cites src/upload.ts:400, but the file has 120 lines. What happens to the finding?

options.text: It stays high, because the skeptic confirmed it
options.why: A confirmation needs a cite that holds. This one points past the end of the file.

options.text: It is treated as unsure and is lowered to medium severity and medium confidence
options.why: A confirmed verdict with a bad cite counts as unsure, which lowers both by one step.

options.text: It is dropped, as if refuted
options.why: Only a refuted verdict drops a finding. A bad cite only weakens it.

p: Byte on agent PRs: fcp's .github/workflows/byte-review.yml adds opened to its pull_request types and lets opened and synchronize through, drafts included, only when github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'rhino-ai-agents[bot]'. Byte's src/gate.ts gets the agent-PR case next to ownWeeklyPr with a new agentAuthors policy list, parseTrigger allows drafts for that case only, and the 60-minute quiet-period nudge is skipped for agent PRs. src/engines.ts adds the AGENT PR clause to the review prompt, and src/review.ts accepts an optional known field and records the count. The byte-review.yml change is also described in Nova's PR work; one ticket must own it.

Posting: an optional category in the output contract, selectInline in src/review.ts, the severity table in the Byte check run, and quietCategories per team in config/repositories.json. The panel: skills/panel/lenses/*.md built from the FE playbook's passes, src/panel.ts with runLenses and skeptic, skills/panel/skeptic.md, and per-lens counts in the run manifest. The requirements lens works from the PR title, body and RH key until Security approves a read-only Jira token for review.yml.

tickets.why: Byte reviews drafts from the agents' App with a valid Requested-by, and reads the receipt as data.
On agent PRs only new high and medium findings go inline; the rest are counted; quiet categories.
The five lenses, three of them blind, each its own read-only session.
Dedupe, then a skeptic per finding that must cite a real file and line.

words.plain: The short summary of Nova's self-review in the PR body: what was found, fixed and left, and why.
A finding that matches an issue the receipt already lists as open; it is counted, not posted.
A kind of finding people mostly reject for a team; on agent PRs it is counted, not posted.
One separate review session with one job, such as correctness or security.
A lens that reads only the diff and the code, never the PR body or the author's plan.
A session that tries to prove each finding wrong and must cite the file and line for its answer.

review.q: From memory: the conditions under which Byte's gate accepts a draft PR.
review.a: The author and the sender are in the agent-authors list (rhino-ai-agents[bot]), the base is main, and the live PR body has a Requested-by: line naming a person with write access today.

review.q: Which findings are counted instead of posted on an agent PR?
review.a: Low findings, known findings from the receipt, and findings in a quiet category, except that a high security or data-loss finding is never quiet.

review.q: What happens to a finding the skeptic answers unsure about?
review.a: Its severity and confidence are lowered one step; the confidence filter then drops it if it fell to low confidence.

remember: On Nova's drafts, Byte posts only what Nova should fix: new high and medium findings that survive the skeptic, while text in the PR can mark a finding known but never make it disappear.
